title: Reverse Linked List
prompt:
Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse it and return the new head.

**Example**: `1→2→3→4→5` → `5→4→3→2→1`.

Move 1 from the pattern lesson: save → flip → advance ×2. This must become pure muscle memory — it's a sub-step of many harder problems.
hints: Every arrow needs to point the other way. But the moment you redirect `curr.next`, you lose your only way to the rest of the list — unless you do something first.
Two travelers: `prev` (starts null) and `curr` (starts at head). Each step turns `curr`'s arrow back toward `prev`, then both move forward one node.
Loop body, exactly this order: `ListNode next = curr.next; curr.next = prev; prev = curr; curr = next;` When curr hits null, `prev` is the new head.

solution.explanation: After each iteration, `prev` heads the already-reversed prefix and `curr` heads the untouched suffix; saving `curr.next` before flipping keeps the suffix reachable. Starting with `prev = null` makes the old head the new tail with no special case, and an empty list returns null naturally. O(n) time, O(1) space (the recursive version uses O(n) stack).
